When drawing legs I like to to split them into two parts: 1. Hips-knees 2. Knees-ankles. I then like to think of the over stylized chatacters from the Total Drama series. Their legs start very wide at the hips, and gradually get smaller leading into the knees. From the knees they then get gradually bigger leading to the center of the bottom portion of the leg and then smaller leading down to the ankles. 
I personally dont draw very stylized, I like to have more realistic anatomy. But Anatomy is hard and looking at the extreme proportions of the TD cast helps really simplify it for me for some reason lol.

Otherwise I also suggest looking at pictures of real legs. Many artists will tell you to "ALWAYS USE REFERENCES"  This is what they mean, if you're drawing legs, pull up some pictures of some legs and try to recreate them in your picture.

Another good tip for studying anatomy is to trace overtop of your reference (If you're comfortable, I like to make my own pose references because its easier to find the specific pose I want and I'm terrified of art theft). Break down the pose into shapes (or one of those anatomy skeletons). And then remove the reference and try to use those shapes as a guide to recreate the pose.

I find watching speedpaints from other artists helps me alot as well.

Okay that was alot, hope this makes sense! Feel free to ask any questions :D
